lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Is there life after being a weapon?

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: You can ask that every day for the rest of your life, or you can find someone who already answered it.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Frostwind Reach. Unmarked stellar chart. There's a dead world here, Cinder Vale. I've stopped here before.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Drive coils are overheating. We're losing power fast. Emergency descent initiated.

lines.speaker: Salvage Pirate 1
lines.text: New wreck! Easy pickings!

lines.speaker: Salvage Pirate 2
lines.text: Come on! They're grounded!

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: This is Ashfall. We don't ask questions.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: We ask forgiveness instead, but first you have to remember why you need it.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: Your pilot took burn-damage from the descent. He's lucky the coils didn't rupture. He's lucky the blast didn't take him.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How far underground are we?

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: Far enough that the Dominion stopped looking for us decades ago. We're below their sensors. Below their reach. The world is dead. The monastery is alive.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: Sela says you woke up without a past.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: That is mercy pretending to be cruelty. But you are welcome here regardless of your history.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I have a name. A designation. The rest is blank.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: Then you have your own choice to make. You may rest in this hall and ask forgiveness of ghosts that may not even remember their names. Or you may work in the Blade Garden and understand the discipline beneath violence.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: Either way, you will do it as yourself. Not as a weapon.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The Blade Garden.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: You fight like someone trying to remember.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I don't remember the training.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: Your body does. Your body remembers everything you've forgotten.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: I have been here five years. Before that I don't talk about. But I know that look, it's the one I had when I arrived. You can see the shape of the cage, but you still think the door is a lie.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: What was your name? Before the monastery?

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: That operative is dead. Don't mourn her. She chose to die here, and something else chose to live instead.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: Overseer Khall is offering a recovery bounty on a lost asset carrying classified neural implants.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: Ronin-7 was the finest of his generation. The failsafe was meant to be merciful. I am offering this bounty not as a sanction, but as a courtesy. He was something worth making.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: He broadcast that knowing I would hear it.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: Khall is hunting you. He always was.

lines.speaker: Dominion Soldier 1
lines.text: Monastery breach! Hostiles engaging in central corridor!

lines.speaker: Dominion Soldier 2
lines.text: Clearing meditation hall! Stand by for thermal scan!

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: The chip in your spine is broadcasting. Not the purge sequence, a secondary function. A locator.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: They allowed you to believe you were free while the leash stayed invisible.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The Dominion never lost me.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: No. They were always watching.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: I was a Dominion architect. One of the early designers of operative conditioning, a precursor to everything later built into your generation.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: I designed the first versions of the locator function. I trained your handler Khall when he was still a boy. I built the machine that is tearing you apart, one second at a time.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: Then I saw what the program became and I faked my own death.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: I came to this place to stop killing. You didn't come for peace, you came because you have nowhere else to go. But I am asking you the same question I once asked myself: will you turn that weapon on the people who built you, or will you learn that putting the sword down is the only real victory?

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: I knew you would come to this place. Every operative eventually looks for a way to stop.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: There is no peace in renunciation, Ronin-7. There is only the lie you tell yourself while the purge continues.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: I built the first version of him. And I will not let you break what is left.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: Your augments are a living record of everything we built. Every syndicate in this galaxy will hunt you for the architecture alone.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: Come back to the Dominion and I can restore your full capacity. You could find out what you were truly made for.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: Or you can stay here and die slowly in the dark, wondering if the peace was real or just the slowest possible form of cruelty.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: You cut yourself open for a signal relay. The purge is still running. You are still dying.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: The beacon was never the leash. The leash is what he believes about himself. But now you have no signal to follow, Overseer. You have no business here.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: You are learning. But you carry ghosts, a massacre, an orphanage, choices made and choices made in your name. You will need to know the difference between them before this is over.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How will I know?

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: You won't, not yet. Build a life anyway. The truth finds you when you are ready to hold it.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: I pulled a body out of the void and it turned out to be a man. I am glad he woke up.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: Before I came here, I served a syndicate that believed peace was weakness. We fought constantly, against three other syndicates, rotating enemies, always funded just enough to keep the killing going.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: I was years into the work before I understood the pattern. The wars never ended. They just rotated. Enemies changed sides. Debts accumulated. And somewhere above all of it, someone was keeping score.

lines.speaker: Sela
lines.text: The Dominion does not rule the galaxies by force alone. It keeps them caged by keeping the syndicates desperate and at war. It seeds the hatred, funds both sides, and collects the debt. Every galaxy is a pit they built to trap the people in it.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Duty, not destiny.

lines.speaker: Morrow
lines.text: To forget is to be cursed. To remember without becoming the thing you remembered, that is to be free.
